extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers interested in philosophy of humor / comedy theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Henri Bergson's criteria for what makes something comic: treating laughter as a social phenomenon, identifying rigidity vs. flexibility, and analysing comic situations, movements, and characters with a systematic method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter as a distinctly human and social phenomenon
rubrics_metrics.description: Bergson examines laughter as a distinctly human and social phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat laughter/comedies as arising in social contexts; evaluate comic material for its relation to human social interaction, community responses, and the social corrective function of laughter. Consider audience and norms when judging whether something is comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy arises from rigidity interrupting life's natural flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy arises from rigidity interrupting life's natural flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify instances where mechanical or rigid behaviour, thought, or form intrudes upon otherwise living, adaptable situations — this contrast is the source of the comic. When producing or evaluating humor, look for that contrast (rigidity vs. fluidity) in actions, timing, language, or circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter serves as a moral corrective
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter serves as a moral corrective, forcing people to recognize their vices and conform to social norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the comic element highlights a vice, absurdity, or social failing and whether it functions to correct or shame that behaviour. Use this as a metric for the social purpose or ethical effect of comedy (not all effective comedy must be corrective, but Bergson treats this as a central function).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze comic situations, movements, and characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Through analyzing comic situations, movements, and characters, Bergson develops a scientific method for understanding the laws governing humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tripartite analytic focus — situations (contexts and events), movements (physical actions and timing), and characters (types, traits, and social roles) — to dissect comedic effect. Evaluate each for the presence of the rigidity/flexibility contrast and their role in producing laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: A systematic/scientific method for the laws of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Bergson develops a scientific method for understanding the laws governing humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a systematic, law-seeking approach rather than relying on intuition alone: identify recurring mechanisms, formal conditions, and generalizable principles (e.g., mechanical rigidity in living contexts) that produce the comic. This is a criterion for rigorous analysis of humor.
